GK-03.c01: This module is law, not driving skill: most questions ask for a number, so memorize the **bold** numbers.
Rules marked **[CA]** are California rules; **CVC** = California Vehicle Code, CFR = federal rules, CHP = California Highway Patrol.
**GVWR** = gross vehicle weight rating, the maker's maximum safe weight for the loaded vehicle.
[CA] Some California rules are taught in other modules, and **triple trailers** are not legal in California.
GK-03.c02: Out-of-state traffic conviction (not parking), in any vehicle → tell your licensing agency within **30 days**.
License suspended, revoked, cancelled or disqualified → tell your employer within **2 business days** (answer this on the test for the 1.4 wording).
H endorsement holder with a disqualifying crime, mental commitment, or giving up citizenship → notify the issuing state and surrender the H within **24 hours**.
Hold only **1 license**; no holding a phone to talk, dialing only with **one button**, and no sending or reading texts.
Always wear a seat belt: if you are thrown from the vehicle without one, you are **4 times** more likely to be killed.
GK-03.c03: Major offenses (alcohol, drugs, BAC **0.04%**+ in a CMV, leaving the scene, felony): 1st = **1 year** (3 years with HazMat); 2nd = life.
A felony involving a controlled substance → **life** on the 1st conviction, in any vehicle.
Serious traffic offenses: 2nd within 3 years = **60 days**; 3rd within 3 years = **120 days**.
Railroad crossing offenses: at least **60 days**, then 120 days, then 1 year (2nd and 3rd within 3 years).
1st out-of-service order violation → at least **90 days** (up to 1 year); hauling HazMat or 16+ passengers → at least **180 days** (up to 2 years).
GK-03.c04: [CA] Every CMV must stop at **each posted CHP inspection and testing site**, because scales and inspections find unsafe or overweight trucks.
[CA] An officer who suspects an unsafe or oversize load may stop, inspect, measure or weigh you, and make you **reload or remove** part of it.
[CA] Driving illegally over a highway or bridge makes you liable for all damage; the **owner and the driver** may both have to pay.
GK-03.c05: [CA] CARB rules cover every commercial diesel vehicle in California, **even ones based in another state or country**.
[CA] Diesel CMVs over **10,001 lb** GVWR may idle at most **5 minutes** when not needed, and not at all at a school.
[CA] Truck and Bus Regulation (over **14,000 lb**): DPF since Jan 1, 2012; since **2020** DMV won't register a truck that doesn't comply.
[CA] Smoke inspection (PSIP): fleets of 2+ diesel trucks test **every year** and keep records at least **2 years**; DPF trucks have a 5% opacity limit.
[CA] Port (drayage) trucks over 26,000 lb must be in the CARB Drayage Truck Registry with a **2007** or newer engine.
GK-03.c06: [CA] A single vehicle may be at most **40 ft** long; semitrailers, buses and housecars can be exempt under certain conditions.
[CA] The front bumper may stick out no more than **2 ft** ahead of the fenders, cab or radiator.
[CA] An articulated bus or trolley coach may be at most **60 ft** long.
[CA] Buses may add a **1 ft** safety bumper, an 18 in front wheelchair lift, and bike racks up to 36 in front or 10 ft rear.
GK-03.c07: [CA] Truck tractor + one trailer → total length at most **65 ft**.
[CA] Truck tractor + semitrailer + trailer (doubles) → at most **75 ft**, and neither trailer longer than **28 ft 6 in**.
[CA] Cities and counties may post signs banning combinations longer than **60 ft** on their roads.
[CA] Load length, from the farthest-forward point to the farthest-back point of vehicle or load, is at most **75 ft**.
GK-03.c08: [CA] Long one-piece loads (poles, timbers, pipes, structural parts) may be up to **80 ft** on a pole or pipe dolly or semitrailer.
[CA] A load may extend at most **3 ft** past the front bumper or front tires; a load made only of vehicles may extend **4 ft**.
[CA] Rear overhang on a single vehicle is at most **2/3 of the wheelbase** behind the last point of support, because a long tail swings wide.
Example: wheelbase 18 ft → load may hang out at most 2/3 × 18 = **12 ft** behind the last support.
GK-03.c09: [CA] Body of the vehicle or the load may be at most **102 in (8½ ft)** wide; wheel to wheel with air tires, **108 in (9 ft)**.
[CA] Permitted devices (door handles, chain binders) may stick out **3 in** each side; required devices (lights, mirrors) **10 in** each side.
[CA] Special mobile or construction equipment and loosely piled farm products (load plus racks) may be **120 in** wide.
[CA] Buses are limited to **102 in** (city or suburban for-hire buses 104 in); local roads may ban vehicles wider than **96 in (8 ft)**.
GK-03.c10: [CA] Implements of husbandry (**farm equipment**) are generally exempt from width and length limits when moved on a highway during normal farm work.
[CA] A **Caltrans transportation permit** may still be needed to move farm equipment.
GK-03.c11: [CA] The vehicle and load may be at most **14 ft** high, measured from the road surface.
[CA] Exceptions: **double-deck buses** up to 14 ft 3 in, and farm equipment moved over a highway during farm work.
Why: bridges, overpasses and wires limit how tall a vehicle can safely be.
GK-03.c12: [CA] **Caltrans** may post bridge and highway weight limits that are higher or lower than normal CVC limits.
[CA] Cities and counties may post higher or lower limits on their own roads and bridges and name other routes for heavy vehicles.
[CA] A local weight sign still lets you use the street **by the direct route** to pick up or deliver goods, deliver permitted construction materials, or do utility work.
GK-03.c13: [CA] Single vehicle, in the handbook's wording: **20,000 lb** on the wheels at one end of an axle (20,500 lb for buses) and **10,500 lb** on any one axle.
[CA] The 10,500-lb limit does not apply to **livestock** haulers; never exceed the tire maker's load limit on the sidewall.
[CA] In a combination, any one axle may carry at most **18,000 lb** and the wheels at one end of an axle at most **9,500 lb**.
[CA] A front steering axle in a combination may carry up to **12,500 lb**.
[CA] Groups of 2+ axles use CVC tables: one table if first-to-last axle is **18 ft or less**, another if it is more than 18 ft.
GK-03.c14: [CA] Log trucks have special weight limits, but that extra weight is **not allowed on interstate highways**.
[CA] Weight-to-axle ratio: axles close together = **less weight** allowed; axles spread out = more, because roads carry only so much weight per foot.
[CA] Two tandem sets **36 ft or more** apart may carry **34,000 lb** each, and 68,000 lb together.
GK-03.c15: [CA] Load limits are **not enforced** while you load or unload at, or right next to, a loading or unloading area.
[CA] You may not change a special permit route; the only detour is on **nonresidential streets** to avoid breaking a local city rule.
[CA] Leaving the permitted route with an extralegal load without a peace officer's approval is a **misdemeanor**.
GK-03.c16: [CA] CHP first allows a **200-lb** variation factor; if still **100 lb or more** over after that, you get a citation.
[CA] After a citation you must adjust the load or get an overweight permit **before moving on**.
Example (limit 34,000 lb): 34,250 → 50 over after allowance, no citation; 34,350 → **150** over, citation.
[CA] An overweight **HazMat** load may continue as loaded if adjusting it cannot be done with reasonable safety.
[CA] Livestock and field-loaded perishables are cited but may continue if a single truck is ≤ **1,000 lb** over per axle or group, or a combination ≤ **2,000 lb** gross.
GK-03.c17: [CA] You need a permit to move any vehicle over the **width, height or weight** limits on a California street or highway.
[CA] Get the permit from **Caltrans** for state highways, or from the city or county for their roads.
[CA] Moving an oversize extralegal load without a permit can bring a **fine, jail, or both**, plus excess-load penalties.
GK-03.c18: [CA] Anyone running a CMV, **for hire or privately**, needs a Motor Carrier Permit (MCP) from the DMV.
[CA] For the MCP, a CMV includes a motor truck with **2 or more axles** and a GVWR **over 10,000 lb**, or any vehicle carrying property for hire.
[CA] Not counted: household goods carriers, **pickup trucks**, and 2-axle daily rental trucks under 26,001 lb used non-commercially.
Interstate or foreign carriers hauling property must register under **UCR** (Unified Carrier Registration Act of 2005).
GK-03.c19: [CA] **55 mph** is the top speed for trucks with 3+ axles, **any vehicle towing**, school buses with pupils, farm labor vehicles with passengers, explosives, and trailer buses.
[CA] All other vehicles: **65 mph** on most highways, 55 mph on two-lane undivided highways unless posted higher, **70 mph** only where signed.
Driving so slowly that you block normal traffic is also illegal, unless needed for safety, the law, or your vehicle's size and weight.
Example: a pickup towing a small trailer is limited to **55 mph**, because heavy and towed loads need more distance to stop.
GK-03.c20: [CA] 55-mph-list vehicles use the signed lanes; with no signs, drive in the **right-hand lane** or as near the right edge as possible.
[CA] On a divided highway with **4 or more lanes** in your direction, you may also use the lane just left of the right lane.
Why: slow, heavy vehicles stay out of the faster left lanes, so traffic flows with fewer lane-change conflicts.
GK-03.c21: [CA] The lane rule does not apply when preparing to **turn**, entering or leaving a highway, or using another lane to stay on your route.
[CA] Buses (not school or trailer buses) may use **any lane** if they are not towing.
[CA] Larger trucks leave the designated system only at signed exits, going to a **terminal** or up to **1 mile** for food, fuel, lodging or repairs.
GK-03.c22: [CA] On a two-lane highway where passing is unsafe, a slow vehicle with **5 or more vehicles** behind must pull off to let them pass.
[CA] Use the nearest **signed turnout** or any other place with enough room, because drivers stuck behind a slow truck may try a dangerous pass.
GK-03.c23: [CA] **Intrastate** (inside California only) → follow California hours of service; **interstate** → follow federal hours of service.
You are interstate if cargo came from or is going out of state, or is hazardous substances or wastes.
You can be **interstate without leaving California**, for example hauling freight from Arizona from a Los Angeles warehouse to Fresno.
GK-03.c24: A record of duty status logs **all** your hours: driving, on duty not driving, off duty, and sleeper berth.
**Each driver and each co-driver** keeps the log in duplicate.
Show it **immediately** when asked by an authorized CHP employee, a salaried police officer, or a deputy sheriff.
GK-03.c25: [CA] California intrastate: drive at most **12 hours** after 10 off, and no driving after **16 hours** on duty; federal is 11 hours and the 14th hour.
[CA] California: no driving after **80 hours** on duty in any 8 days (farm products 112); federal: 60 hours in 7 days or **70 hours in 8 days**.
Both systems need **10 hours** off in a row before driving again; the sleeper berth split is 2 periods, one at least 8 hours.
Bad weather adds **2 hours** of driving; in California never more than 14 hours driving or after 16 hours on duty.
Federal carriers restart the 7/8-day period after **34+ hours** off in a row; limits exist because tired drivers react slowly.
GK-03.c26: [CA] A crash in California causing death, injury, or damage **over $1,000** → report it to the DMV on form SR 1 within **10 days**.
[CA] The SR 1 is required whether or not you caused the crash, **even on private property**, and in addition to police or insurance reports.
[CA] If you do not file a required SR 1, your **driving privilege will be suspended**.
[CA] Tell your employer within **5 days** after a crash in the employer's vehicle, or immediately if the employer requires it.
GK-03.c27: [CA] General freight in vehicles of **10,001 lb** or more → at least **$750,000** combined single limit; 10,000 lb or less → $300,000.
[CA] Oil, HazMat, or waste → **$1,000,000** CSL; top-risk loads like explosives or poison gas → **$5,000,000** CSL.
[CA] Proof must stay on file while the MCP is active; if the insurance or bond lapses, the **DMV suspends the MCP**.
[CA] A driver must be able to show financial responsibility **before operating** the vehicle.
GK-03.c28: Interstate vehicles needing a CDL must register under **IRP** (apportioned plates and cab card) and **IFTA** (fuel tax) with their base jurisdiction.
They qualify with **2 axles over 26,000 lb**, **3 or more axles** at any weight, or a combination over 26,000 lb; recreational vehicles are excluded.
IFTA uses one license and **one quarterly tax return** filed with your base jurisdiction.
Record the odometer at the start of the day, when **leaving a state or province**, and at trip or day end; keep a receipt for every fuel purchase.
Keep IVDR (trip report) records at least **4 years**, because fees and taxes are calculated from them and can be audited.
